 ORDER (Made by the Hon'ble Chief Justice) We have heard Mr.K.Balu, learned counsel for the petitioner,
Mrs.R.Anitha, learned Special Government Pleader, for respondents 1 to 3 and Mr.AR.L.Sundaresan, learned Senior Counsel for Mr.Pawan Jhabakh for respondents 4 and 5.
2.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the land bearing S.Nos.303/1 and 304/5 situated at Orappam village are classified as Grama Natham and Santhaipettai in the revenue records.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
The respondent Nos.4 and 5 have encroached upon the said land.
The land is used for religious purposes.

Even as per the revenue records, the land is classified under Board Standing Order 15A of the Standing Orders of the Board of Revenue meaning that it comes under the temporary occupation for agricultural workers.
According to the learned counsel, the respondents be directed to verify the said land.
The stand of the respondents that they are patta lands is incorrect.
3. The respondent No.2 has filed the status report.

The respondent No.2 has affirmed the facts in paras 6 and 8 to 10, which read thus:

It is submitted that the compensation amount for the above lands acquired for N a t i o n a l H i g h w a y s , w e r e p a i d t o T m t . P e r i a p p a @ L a k s h m i https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis w/o Kaverigounder, whose husband Thiru.Kaverigounder purchased an extent of 0.07 acres in S.No.303/1 by virtue of registered purchase deed No.1692 dated 23.09.1972 from Thiru Krishnasamy Bandhulu and the petioners herein, by the Special District Revenue Officer, who was the Land Acquisition Officer as per Award No.1849/2010 B2 dated:28.2.2013.
9.

It is submitted that from the above, it maykindly be seen that the S.Nos.303/1B2 and 304/5B of Orappam village, Bargur Taluk, Krishnagiri District, are continue as patta lands and that they are not classified as Grama Natham and Santhaipettai,
respectively, as claimed by the petitioner.
10.

It is submitted that there are one Mariamman Temple facing east, one Vinayagar temple facing north, one terraced residential building and grocery shop, a hotel roofed with sheets and 4 tararind trees existing in S.No.303/1B2.

In S.No.304/5B,
there is one drinking water tank of cattle, one square well, one defuct bore well with hand pump and one palm tree existing.
Besides, a weekly Shandy is being conducted on every Wednesday in the above patta lands.
The Field Measurement Book (FMB) of S.No.303/1B2 bears a writ up as Grama Nathan and the same was also scored out.

Probably, in the above circumstances, the petitioner might have come to a conclusion that the above lands are Government Poramboke lands and that he has filed this writ petition with a prayer for a direction to remove the encroachments in the above lands, before this Hon'ble Court.
It is submitted that the FMB is not an adequate record to conclude about the classification of any land.
It is the 'A' Register, which specifically discloses about the classification of any land.

In respect of S.Nos.303/1B2 and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 304/5B, the 'A' Register, both prior and after the Updating of Survey conducted in the year 1984, specifically discloses that the above lands are patta lands.

Therefore, acceptance of the prayer of the petitioner for a direction to the respondents 1 to 3 to take action and remove the encroachment made by the 4th respondent in S.No.303/1 and 304/5, does not arise in this case, for the reason that the above lands are patta lands and that they are not poramboke lands as imaginarily claimed by the petitioner.
4. The averments made in the status report are supported by documents.
If anyone is aggrieved by the grant of patta, then the aggrieved person can challenge the same in the appropriate proceedings as provided under the Patta Passbook Act.
In the present case, we do not find any case for entertaining the writ petition.
The writ petition is dismissed.
There will be no order as to costs.
(S.V.G., CJ.)
